records.title: Does the A-03 image audit bound missed doubled runes?
records.question: Does the source's preserved image-count audit satisfy its declared controls and justify K≤26 missed doublets?
records.reader_question: Could missed doubled runes explain the repeat deficit?
records.summary: The published counts and arithmetic reproduce, but the source misses its image agreement gate and its arithmetic-only planted control does not measure image detection. The observed excess of 26 pairs is not an upper bound on hidden merges.
records.finding: The classifier reports 99.4146% agreement against a 99.5% gate. Its source code loads 13,381 component rows but does not process them in the K control. The saved counts give 108−82=26 excess image pairs and a stated threshold of 93 additional pairs; without a measured error bound, the first number cannot cap the latter.

scope.representation: Pinned Dukotah Round10 classifier output, log and Round16/A-03 source receipt, not original image pixels.
scope.procedure: Hash-check six source files, parse classifier agreement and count log, recompute the source threshold and arithmetic K control, inspect whether source code actually reprocesses glyph rows, and give a finite nonnegative error assignment with the same observed surplus.
scope.parameters: Source image agreement gate 99.5%; source comparison floor 1.38%; source counts as preserved at f08b20b.
scope.exclusions: No fresh image transcription, no measured classifier error rate for merged glyphs, no general autokey exclusion.

records.limitations: This is an audit of saved source receipts and inference, not an independent reading of the source images or a test of every autokey variant. A constructed error assignment shows logical possibility, not empirical plausibility.

records.title: Alberti branch proposal: LP2-39 row and modulo-31 arithmetic
records.question: Do the source's identified LP2-39 row, 4–5–4 shift sums and claimed modulo-31 matches reproduce as written?
records.summary: The 19-rune row and four signed short-group sums reproduce. Standard modulo 31 turns the right totals −33 and −39 into 29 and 23, rather than the claimed positive 2 and 8; the proposed disk reading remains untested.
records.finding: The identified row has 19 runes in groups of 3, 4, 6, 5 and 1. Left raw short sums −13 and −17 and right raw short sums −33 and −39 reproduce. The right pair reduces modulo 31 to 29 and 23, not the source's +2 and +8; obtaining the positive pair requires an additional direction reversal. The proposed deciphering rule cannot be checked from these arithmetic inputs.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-39 UTF-8 rune transcription and the source's two explicit 13-number plant arrays, short overlay and posted final arrays, copied into a fixed plan. Source transcript identified by SHA-256, not republished.
scope.procedure: Recount the source-identified row's rune groups; calculate the two four-element overlaid short sums and all posted 4–5–4 final-array sums; reduce the signed values using standard nonnegative modulo-31 residues. Repeat short sums at all 13 cyclic starts for each plant array as a sensitivity diagnostic.
scope.parameters: One LP2-39 row; two posted 13-number arrays; one posted four-number overlay; fixed groups 4, 5, 4; 13 starting positions for each array; modulus 31. No fitted key, symbol mapping or selected plaintext.
scope.exclusions: Complete Alberti disk alphabets, rule-state transitions, branch inheritance, letter assembly, word-selection search, full-page reading, or a chance probability for the source's selected interpretation. The separate method files and diagrams referred to in the discussion are not available as pinned inputs here.

records.limitations: The transcript states the arrays but does not supply a complete fixed disk configuration and transition table. Its group and target choices were made during an evolving exploration, so the 13-rotation check is sensitivity analysis, not a statistical null. It cannot validate or refute the purported LP2-39 plaintext.

records.title: Alternating alphabets with two interruption clocks
records.question: Do two known keys, alternating GP/reversed-GP cipher alphabets and either of two ciphertext-F pause rules recover a declared page opening?
records.reader_title: Can switching alphabets and pausing at F recover a known opening?
records.reader_intro: Uses two keys from solved passages while switching between the normal and reversed rune alphabets, testing whether F pauses the key position alone or also pauses the alphabet switch.
records.reader_question: Could F pause the key, the alphabet, or both?
records.summary: Neither F-clock rule recovered a declared twelve-rune opening in 55 LP2 pages.
records.finding: Neither way of pausing at an F rune produced any of the nine predicted twelve-rune beginnings on the 55 tested pages. One rule paused just the key; the other also paused the switch between alphabets.

scope.representation: First twelve GP29 runes, including headings, of LP2-00–55; omit runeless LP2-50. Page-local state. Other characters do not advance it.
scope.procedure: Alternate ordinary/reversed cipher alphabets, each with its own known repeating key. Decode F normally but hold the selected key position there. Compare always-toggling versus F-paused alphabet clocks; compare each head with nine fixed twelve-rune known-reading openings.
scope.parameters: 2 key assignments × 104 phase pairs × 2 first alphabets × 2 signs × 2 clock policies = 1,664 settings; 55 pages; 823,680 exact comparisons. 1,664 roundtrips on 87 prescribed runes plus 1,664 forced-marker controls.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, cipher alphabet permutations, literal/removed F, other interruption runes, word resets, additional layers, noninitial starts and unknown plaintext openings. No historical exact-method replay is claimed.

records.title: Autokey with skipped key positions
records.question: Does the complete source autokey-with-skips grid produce a full-page candidate above its English-score gate?
records.reader_question: Can recovered or encrypted runes continue a key when positions may be skipped?
records.summary: No candidate crossed the source English-score threshold in 9,900 full-page decodes. The source encoder and decoder follow different future-key rules in 247 of 360 known-message tests, limiting the result.
records.finding: None of the 9,900 full-page outputs passed the English-score gate. But 247 of 360 known-message tests used different rules in the source encoder and decoder, so this does not rule out autokey.

scope.representation: Pinned GP29 indices,55 source segments/12,956 runes; page-local forward order. P key is primer plus that hypothesis recovered plaintext; C key is primer plus complete observed ciphertext, padded with zeros as source. Exact transcription remains external.
scope.procedure: Execute run_full_new.run_autokey semantics with unchanged P/C decoder rules. Stable cumulative-score beam returns first winner; gate its source normalized English score. Separately find first normalized maximum among retained terminal hypotheses, without changing the returned source output. Preserve all cases and control failures.
scope.parameters: 29 singleton indices plus 16 literal source words =45 distinct primers; P/C models x signs -1/+1 x 55 segments =9,900 full calls. Beam 450/max_skip 3/strict score > -5.5; no target short screen or Atbash. P frontier total skips <= primer length-1, so 3,190 singleton-P labels are rigid. Source encoder controls suppression 0.83,360 fixed seeded cases/two known readings; all outcomes retained.
scope.exclusions: Other primers/offsets/alphabets, resets inside pages, joined pages, other languages, altered encoder/frontier rules or ranking, paths discarded by the source beam and global-null significance. No general cipher-family exclusion; 247 source-generated known truths are invalid under their matching decoder.

records.limitations: Historical source-algorithm diagnostic, not a validated autokey-family exclusion. Known-message cases reuse two passages; 247 generated truths are inadmissible under their paired decoder. Source P can skip at most primer length minus one draws; singleton P is rigid. C encoder substitutes zero for unavailable ciphertext while decoder reads the observed stream. Source gates pass on 90 runes, not the full target regime. No new global-null probability, other primers, alphabets, offsets, languages, joined pages or discarded beam-path recovery.

scope.parameters: 2,165 seeds × 16 generators × 5 reductions × two directions × two signs × two Atbash states = 1,385,600 configurations; zero offset; at most three rejected draws per emitted rune; all 55 nonempty LP2 page starts; nine fixed 12-rune cribs.
scope.exclusions: No different seeds or hashes, nonzero offsets, independent page keys, word resets, alternative transcriptions, other plaintexts or original source English-scoring claims.

records.title: Does a matching decoder recover the planted message?
records.question: Do matching source decoder rules recover known planted text across the eight C2-EXT generator-and-plant pairs when supplied the correct key?
records.reader_question: Can a decoding tool miss the right message even with the right key?
records.summary: Matching the decoder to the planted rule raises median recovery from 10–33% to 98–100% across eight source generator-and-plant pairs. All source recovery gates pass.
records.finding: With the right key supplied, a decoder that matches the planted rule recovered 98–100% of runes at the median; the comparison decoder recovered 10–33%.

scope.representation: Source-derived English GP29 plaintext, correct generator streams, planted ciphertext and decoded rune paths; no manuscript candidate.
scope.procedure: Regenerate all 56 exact source fixtures, run unchanged matching/baseline source beams, compare every archived score and recovery, independently count rune matches and rescore all paths.
scope.parameters: Eight generator-and-plant pairs × seven seeds 3301–3307 × two decoders; 240 runes; width 400; sign -1; offset 0; suppression .83; paired skips or q=.05 / ten fixed drifts; median recovery gate .90.
scope.exclusions: Manuscript sweep, wrong-key calibration, native runtime parity, nonzero-offset recovery, other lengths or languages and general cipher exclusion.

records.limitations: Finite known-key English-derived plants at 240 runes; seven fixed seeds per pair. No wrong-key calibration or manuscript sweep. records.title: A column solver with a short-key limit

records.finding: This short-key solver produced no English-like LP2 output. It recovered the planted passage in 107 of 165 page-and-key-length settings; the other 58 did not recover it. Shuffled searches often scored higher than the best manuscript result.

scope.representation: Archived GP29 rune order including headings; source pages17–72 aligned to site LP2-00–55, with LP2-50 excluded because its pinned transcription has no runes.

Plant exact known texts and repeat the full 165-setting search on199 pagewise shuffled controls.
scope.parameters: 3 fixed periods ×55 rune-bearing pages =165 outputs; 9 complete-reading plants, 165 page-length plants, 199 full-search shuffle replicates, English line −5.5.
scope.exclusions: No other fixed periods, KL0 target verdict, source alternate patched/rune/Latin key transforms, modified interrupter list, other languages or key layers.

records.limitations: Only fixed KL2,3,5 and the direct numeric preview were scored as English. records.title: Long-key search with optional skipped positions
records.question: Does a pinned beam search over three long candidate keys recover complete text from six unsolved LP2 pages?

records.summary: The archived 54-case beam search reproduces and finds no score above its −5 bar. In 18 planted collision-skip cases with the correct key, all scores clear that bar but none recover the exact text, so the source screen cannot exclude the proposed mechanism.
records.finding: None of the tested long-text keys produced a candidate passing the English-language check. But the decoder also failed to recover any of the 18 complete known messages planted with skipped key positions, even though all passed that language check.

scope.representation: Pinned krisyotam rune-only source segments, which agree exactly with site rune sequences. The rune-free LP2-50 segment is omitted; tested source indices are identical to listed site page IDs.

records.title: Number-grid bytes as a key with skipped positions

records.summary: The exact published page search scores 880 fixed settings; none clears its −5.5 screen. The same decoder exactly recovers 16 of 16 planted complete known readings. The result concerns this byte-to-key rule and the executable source padding behavior.
records.finding: Using the number-grid bytes as a key produced no candidate that passed the English-language check on the 55 tested pages. The decoder did recover all 16 short messages with known answers.

scope.representation: Pinned source rune-only transcription; its 55 unsolved segments match LP2-00–55 excluding rune-free LP2-50 exactly. Two committed 256-byte grid readings, forward or reversed, become GP29 key values by byte modulo 29.
scope.procedure: Run the original payload_skip.py from pinned commit f08b20b in a temporary copy. scope.parameters: Four payload byte streams × two signs × two Atbash flags × 55 nonempty pages = 880 whole-page cases; offset zero, source beam width 320, at most three skipped values per rune, source score screen >−5.5. The source repeats payload bytes enough to cover initial page length and zero-pads beyond that array.
scope.exclusions: No alternate stem readings of the grid, nonzero key offsets, whole-corpus decoding, other page or text layers, arbitrary byte transformations, indefinitely cycling key positions after skips, or other Campaign XVIII branches.

records.limitations: The original generic wrong-key gate cannot finish because its Mabinogion file is absent, though its correct-key part and our payload-specific plants pass. records.title: Grid prefix channels as repeating rune keys
records.question: Do suffix streams split by the grid's leading digit recover a known 12-rune opening at an LP2 page start?
records.reader_question: Have the five grid-prefix groups been tried as separate keys?
records.summary: Five suffix channels, three declared value mappings, both Vigenère signs and every real key phase gave no exact known opening at the start of any of 55 nonempty LP2 pages.
records.finding: The channels have 60, 58, 65, 56 and 17 suffixes. Across 58,190 named page configurations and 523,710 fixed 12-rune opening comparisons, none matched. The longest partial opening prefix was three runes. The 17 group-4 hex nibbles were used as 17 values, not padded to bytes; their direct values duplicate the group-4 base-60-digit key.

scope.representation: Source grid: all 256 two-character tokens from LP2-49–51 in printed sequence. Targets: first 12 rune indices on all 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages; nine fixed 12-rune known-reading openings. Source paths and hashes are pinned in plan.json.
scope.procedure: Partition tokens by leading digit 0–4, retaining suffix order. Map suffixes to base-60 digit values modulo 29 or ASCII byte values modulo 29; for group 4 also parse 17 individual hexadecimal nibbles. Use each as a repeating GP29 key under both signs at every phase. Compare first 12 output indices exactly with each fixed opening.
scope.parameters: Channel lengths 60/58/65/56/17; 1,058 named mapping/phase/sign settings including 34 group-4 duplicate settings; 55 target pages; nine openings; 58,190 named page cases and 523,710 exact comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Unspecified prefix-as-direction table and route, bytes formed from an odd nibble count, later ciphertext offsets, key skips, word resets, cross-page state, other alphabets and language scoring.

records.limitations: Only page-start, uninterrupted repeating-key GP29 Vigenère with two signs was tested. The nine openings are fixed known readings, not a language score. records.summary: The 59-symbol count reproduces, but symbol count alone does not determine a radix. A custom alphabet deleting f yields valid base-59 bytes; the conventional digit order requires base 60 for a byte-per-pair interpretation.

records.summary: For exact adjacent duplicate insertions, all 28 nonzero rune-difference counts are unchanged. Even an artificial 20-count allowance reaches CV 0.066 against the source's 0.40 signal bar.
records.finding: The pinned transcription yields 9,640 within-word pairs, 60 doublets and nonzero difference CV 0.0608. scope.parameters: 9,640 adjacent pairs, 60 doublets; 28 nonzero diagonals; k=0..40, with the source decision at k=20; CV signal bar 0.40, safe bar 0.30.

records.title: Can one score cutoff judge every decode?
records.question: Under the original source beam and English model, how do planted recovery, text register and length/beam setting affect the interpretation of a fixed −5.5 cutoff?

records.summary: Four of 28 synthetic decodes pass the English-score cutoff while recovering less than 90% of the planted text. Five source text registers and three fresh conditional-null settings show why the same cutoff needs matched controls.
records.finding: Four synthetic decodes passed the score cutoff while recovering less than 90% of the known text. The score ranges also changed across text registers and decoder settings, so a score alone cannot certify a correct reading.

scope.representation: Fixed source-derived GP29 plaintext/ciphertext/key fixtures, English quadgram counts and a source ciphertext prefix used only for order-destroying conditional controls.
scope.procedure: Replay the unchanged source beam on fifteen paired register plants and twenty-eight mechanism plants; generate 120 fixed-seed shuffled-prefix nulls per setting; independently recalculate rune recovery, quadgram scores and null summaries.
scope.parameters: Five registers × three L120 trials with correct and wrong keys; four mechanisms × seven L240 plants; source beam width 400/max_skip 3; score cutoff −5.5 and recovery reference 90%; three null settings L31/bw120,L120/bw400,L400/bw120 × 120 draws.
scope.exclusions: Full 67-case L7 envelope; original missing EN_MODERN/CY and derived vowel panels; six-model archive rescoring; G3 difference-floor census; independently preregistered corpus selection; large-search tail calibration; real LP2 keys or cipher exclusions.

records.limitations: Finite source-derived controls, not an LP2 key search. Missing original modern-English/Mabinogion and Welsh inputs and derived vowel-deletion panels are excluded. Five available registers include two English texts, not five languages. Null settings change both length and beam width and have only 120 draws each; the eleven-point tail estimates do not calibrate a large-search error rate. records.title: Does the missing-doublet pattern resemble a lag-one filter?
records.question: Does the unsolved LP2 stream distinguish a continuous lag-one repeat filter from tested recency, rebalancing and line-reset controls calibrated to the same repeat rate?
records.reader_question: Was the repeat-avoidance rule applied to the whole rune stream?
records.summary: The 86 residual adjacent repeats match a continuous lag-one-only filter better than the tested recency/rebalancing or line-reset controls. The comparison cannot distinguish computer code from a person applying the identical rule to otherwise machine-like symbols.
records.finding: Independent input measurements reproduce the 86/12,955 lag-one repeat rate, 3.488% lag-2–8 equality, 0.936 window-58 chi-square per degree of freedom, and 4/86 line-crossing repeats. In the source's 200-replicate matched-control ladder, models with extra recent-symbol avoidance or window rebalancing are distinguishable and rejected; the line-reset model is also distinguishable and rejected. The no-extra-effect hand rung has combined discrimination power 0.110 and remains unresolved.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited LP2 segments of pinned UTF-8 rune transcription, concatenated in page order; slash and page markers retained for line-scope comparisons. 12,956 runes, 55 pages, 594 nonempty physical lines, 648 occupied source line ordinals.
scope.procedure: Independently parse raw runes and reproduce lag equalities, repeat gaps, window chi-square, line-crossing doublets and page dispersion. Freshly run the pinned source fingerprint/controls script with 200 replicates, all controls calibrated to the manuscript lag-one repeat rate, and verify its gate, powered model ladder and scope test.
scope.parameters: 29-rune alphabet; lags 1–8; windows 29/58/116/290; 200 source replicates per modeled family; six hand-model rungs plus uniform, continuous filter and line-reset controls; acceptance interval central 95%; minimum discriminator power 0.80.
scope.exclusions: Other transcription layers, alternative human or machine generators not in the source ladder, an exact cipher/key, the physical identity of the author or pad entropy source.

records.limitations: This is a bounded comparison among specified generators, not proof of a literal machine implementation or entropy source. Controls are calibrated to the observed adjacent-repeat rate. The model ladder does not cover every human strategy; a continuous hand-applied lag-one rule on machine-like symbols is observationally equivalent here. The source counts 648 occupied slash/page line ordinals, whereas the text contains 594 nonempty physical lines.

records.title: Do page-break word joins change the six-rune pattern?
records.question: How much do the 32 rune-to-rune LP2 page edges change word-internal lag-six affine counts if they are joined instead of split?
records.summary: The two fixed page-break conventions give 77/1,267 and 80/1,290 lag-six formula matches. The 32 possible joins add 23 eligible pairs and three matches; adjacent within-word doublets stay at 63.
records.finding: Splitting gives 2,928 tokens, 1,267 lag-six opportunities, 77 matches and 63 within-word adjacent doublets. Joining gives 2,896 tokens, 1,290 opportunities, 80 matches and 63 doublets. The rune count remains 12,956.

scope.representation: Archived raw page text and stored 29-rune order; 55 adjacent page edges. No new image adjudication of word joins.
scope.procedure: Use the same hyphen/period word delimiters as the published lag-six experiment, first forcing page breaks and then concatenating pages; count word tokens, six-rune affine matches and adjacent doublets. List each edge's contribution and independently reparse structured page records.
scope.parameters: LP2-00–55, 29 runes, lag 6, formula c′=24−2c modulo 29; slash and newline are layout only; page breaks either always split or join when both ends are runes.
scope.exclusions: Alternative punctuation rules, page image adjudication, revised transcription layers, a new null-model test, cipher identification.

records.limitations: A rune on both sides of a page edge is not evidence of an intended word join. Both variants are bounds under one archived transcription and one punctuation rule. The published shuffle reference was not recalculated for the joined variant.

scope.representation: Full GP29 rune streams including headings from 55 rune-bearing LP2-00–55 pages; for each pair use the first min(page lengths) runes.

records.limitations: IoC measures symbol concentration, not readable plaintext. The result only assesses zero-offset, common-prefix, nonrepeating direct addition/subtraction; other alignments or cipher layers remain untested.

records.title: How many periodic affine keys can fit a twelve-rune opening?
records.question: For nine fixed known-reading openings and periods 1–8, how many invertible affine keys fit the first twelve runes of each LP2 page, and how much of the following text is determined?
records.reader_question: Can I make a periodic affine key fit an opening, and would that fit mean anything?
records.summary: Period-specific affine constraints were counted exactly across 3,960 fixed page, opening and period combinations, then checked for how many following positions a fit forces.
records.finding: No fixed opening fit periods 1–5. At period 6, 287 of 495 page-opening pairs fit, 276 with one key and 11 with 28. Periods 7 and 8 have 262 and 293 fits respectively, all with many keys: at least 784 and 614,656. Compatible fits at those periods force only 6–9 and 3–6 of the next twelve positions. These are algebraic fits, not readings.

scope.representation: First 24 runes including headings on each rune-bearing LP2-00–55 page; first twelve paired with nine fixed reading openings and next twelve inspected only for forced-position count.
scope.procedure: For each period 1–8, enumerate the 812 invertible GP29 affine maps independently at each residue and retain those satisfying its crib observations; multiply residue counts. Count the following positions whose output is identical under every compatible map for its residue. Verify with a planted period-3 known reading and exhaustive F3 small-field key enumeration.
scope.parameters: 55 pages × 9 fixed openings × 8 periods = 3,960 cases. Each residue has 0, 1 or 28 compatible affine maps after the twelve-rune crib; no whole-key brute force and no language score.
scope.exclusions: No other opening, later alignment, period above 8, key clock reset, mixed alphabet, nonlinear transition, feedback model or historical Alberti branch mechanism.

records.limitations: Only nine proposed twelve-rune openings at page position zero, periods 1–8, invertible GP29 affine maps and archived page text are examined. A contradiction excludes that exact combination only; compatible openings do not establish an encryption method.

records.title: LP2-15 reported reverse-add palindrome: arithmetic and control
records.question: Does the reported 53-digit reverse-add example hold, and how often do its own digits give palindromes after shuffling?
records.summary: The reported 53-digit sum is a palindrome because every mirrored digit pair adds without carrying. The same operation gave a palindrome in 50,442 of 100,000 fixed shuffles of its digit multiset; this does not test the manuscript-to-digits derivation or cipher intent.
records.finding: The quoted sum is correct and palindromic. All 53 mirrored digit-pair sums are at most seven, so no carrying occurs and symmetry is guaranteed. Of 100,000 fixed-digit shuffles, 50,442 produce palindromes under the same integer operation; all 50,442 also satisfy the no-carry condition with a nonzero outer pair.

scope.representation: The exact 53-character decimal string reported for an LP2-15 word-sum-distance construction, including its leading zero; no rune or word transcription is used in this arithmetic-only replay.
scope.procedure: Add the string to its full character reversal as integers, verify all 53 paired decimal columns and carries, then shuffle the fixed digit multiset 100,000 times with seed 3301 and apply the same operation to each.
scope.parameters: One selected 53-character example; 100,000 conditional random permutations; Python random.Random seed 3301; leading zero allowed in shuffled strings.
scope.exclusions: Derivation of GP word sums and nearest-prime distances, alternative zero groupings, a complete search-adjusted p-value, plaintext recovery, and evidence of authorial intent.

records.limitations: The original decimal string and zero grouping were selected before this audit. The source-to-digits derivation has not been replayed, and the conditional shuffle is not a p-value over all available pages, segmentations and arithmetic choices. Computational review only; human review pending.

scope.exclusions: Other moduli or exponents, noncontiguous windows, bit shifts, 54-byte windows built from different grid routes, signatures without these PKCS#1/PSS frame shapes, and verification against a known signed message.

records.title: Complete compression decodes of directly packed LP2 runes
records.question: Do any of the 168 fixed LP2 rune-to-byte streams decode as complete zlib, gzip, raw DEFLATE, bzip2 or XZ data?
records.reader_question: Could directly packed LP2 runes be compressed data?
records.summary: Runs five bounded, full-stream compression decoders on the exact byte streams from the direct rune-packing experiment.
records.finding: All 840 format/stream attempts were invalid: zero complete decompressions among 168 fixed rune-to-byte streams under five formats. No attempt hit the 1 MiB output cap. Known compressed, truncated, trailing-junk and over-limit controls passed for every format; a synthetic rune-packed zlib stream also decoded correctly.

scope.representation: The 168 exact source-record byte streams: 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages and one joined stream, each under index-5-msb, index-5-lsb and prime-byte encoding.
scope.procedure: Verify every reconstructed input SHA-256 against the earlier saved record; run complete-stream zlib, gzip, raw DEFLATE, bzip2 and XZ decoders at offset zero; require EOF, no unused input and output no larger than 1 MiB; independently rebuild bytes from page JSON.
scope.parameters: 168 input streams × five formats = 840 attempts; output cap 1,048,576 bytes; no offsets. Synthetic valid, truncated, trailing-junk and over-limit controls for all five formats, plus one rune-packed zlib fixture.
scope.exclusions: No prefixes, shifted starts, alternate bit widths, token ordering, recursive layers, dictionary search, other formats, unlimited expansion or language scoring.

records.limitations: Only the three fixed rune-to-byte modes and byte-zero complete streams were tested. Compression after an unknown transform, offsets, reordered pages, altered packing, dictionary-assisted decoding, other formats and disputed transcription choices remain outside scope. Invalid decompression does not identify the manuscript's cipher.

records.title: Does a rune-matched scorer improve candidate screening?
records.question: Does the pinned rune-matched quadgram model measurably improve known-reading separation and tighten 200 wrong-key scores?
records.reader_question: Would scoring rune output differently help recognize a real LP reading?
records.summary: Across five known readings the transformed scorer improves scores, but its 200 wrong-key controls have slightly wider rather than narrower spread. Its measured separation gain is 3.6%, not the earlier proposed 18%.
records.finding: The source's five solved-page scores, 200 seed-42 random-key decodes, model size and gates reproduce exactly. The weakest known reading rises from -4.9789 to -4.7744, separation from 28.69 to 29.71 sigma; wrong-key SD rises from 0.0880 to 0.0895, failing the predeclared tightening gate. An independent model reconstruction shows the new quadgram table is exactly the original count table after K/Q->C, V->U and Z->S alias collapse.

scope.representation: Five source-decoded LP1 solved sections (A Warning, Some Wisdom, A Koan, Welcome, Circumference), and A Koan's 742-rune ciphertext parsed from the pinned markdown.
scope.procedure: Replay the source's old and transformed quadgram scorers on identical known texts; score 200 modulo-29 random-key A Koan decodes with Python Random(42); compare the -5.5 known-reading gate, wrong-key SD and sigma separation. Independently rebuild the count tables and scores.
scope.parameters: Five solved pages, 200 random-key decodes, 742 ciphertext runes, seed 42, old vs transformed English quadgram models, -5.5 known-reading gate.
scope.exclusions: Unsolved LP2 ciphertext, other languages, independent held-out scorer training, complete key searches, alternative null samples, or a genuinely rune-unit-aware model.

records.limitations: This is English-scorer calibration, not an unsolved-page cipher test. The 200 wrong keys are one seeded sample on A Koan; the small sampled SD change does not prove a generally noisier model. The source's claimed multi-character rune expansion is not implemented in this particular model construction. A narrative note in the original JSON says +2.9% despite its tabulated values yielding +3.6%.

records.title: How disputed rune readings change the measurements
records.question: If the 450 located O/A/AE machine disagreements were read differently, which manuscript statistics move, and how does one known-key decoder respond to separately simulated transcription errors?
records.reader_question: How much could disputed rune readings change what we measure?
records.summary: Hypothetically replacing all 450 source-suggested O/A/AE alternatives raises joined-stream adjacent repeats from 86 (0.664%) to 103 (0.795%), below the source comparison floor of 126, but shifts normalized IoC from 0.999874 to 1.013823. Known-key LP1 decoder fixtures degrade with separate random ciphertext errors. The reader controls reuse global canonical labels and do not establish independent transcription accuracy. A separately recovered exact KJV input also permits the source's six-level full-book decoder replay; its results are fixture-specific.
records.finding: Changing all 450 proposed rune readings adds 17 adjacent repeats and shifts the frequency statistic. These are hypothetical alternatives, not 450 confirmed errors. In a separate full-length known-key fixture, 450 random changes reduce median recovery to 86%.

scope.representation: Pinned source LP2 pages 0–54 joined as 12,956 GP rune indices. The 450 O/A/AE alternatives are source-reader locations. Separate LP1 planted passages of 120 and 400 runes provide decoder controls. A separate 12,956-rune planted KJV passage is the full-book decoder control.
scope.procedure: Rerun source baseline and 400-trial random, dense and targeted substitution grids; apply all 450 exact alternative readings; rerun source 14-level LP1 decoder grids at 120 and 400 runes; compare numeric source outputs and independently recount repeats and IoC from the pinned stream. Replay the exact source six-level KJV full-book fixture using a recovered hash-matched input; compare every fresh result field with the pinned source output except elapsed seconds.
scope.parameters: 450 unique mapped source alternatives; 400 trials per sampled perturbation level; source fixed seeds/levels; 120×14 L120 and 60×14 L400 LP1 decoder cells; F0 parity gate; source German-corpus comparison floor 0.972% corresponds to 126 repeats. Six KJV full-book error levels [0,50,100,200,450,900] with six replicates each; optional 1–4 level-isolated replay workers.
scope.exclusions: No independent hardcopy image review, strict held-out glyph training, regenerated historical dependency graph, alternative cipher model, or actual LP2 plaintext/key recovery.

records.limitations: The 450 source-reader disagreements are not adjudicated image errors. Source T1 controls are transductive because global canon-derived labels include the test pages. The decoder corrupts synthetic LP1 ciphertext uniformly, not the 450 LP2 locations, and tests one key-skip model with English scoring. The exact full-book KJV fixture was replayed, but uses a different plaintext register as well as length and has six replicates per level. The source dependency graph was not freshly rebuilt. No broad LP2 cipher exclusion follows.

records.title: LP2-00–55: uniform additive keys and adjacent matches
records.question: Does the observed number of within-page adjacent matches agree with independent uniform additive keys modulo 29?
records.reader_title: Would a fresh random shift per rune leave this few repeats?
records.reader_intro: This tests one encryption rule: independently choose one of all 29 alphabet shifts, equally likely, for every rune. It asks whether that rule could reasonably produce as few identical neighbors as LP2 has, rather than testing every kind of key.
records.summary: 86 adjacent matches versus 444.86 expected under one fixed model. Exact lower-tail calculation, page-boundary proof and independent finite controls.
records.finding: The observed 86 matches among 12,901 edges strongly disagree with this uniform model: expected 12,901/29 ≈ 444.86; conditional P(D≤86) ≈ 1.0708e-98. This is not logical impossibility or a probability about language.

scope.representation: Archived rune-only page streams; headings included; remove non-runes; count overlapping equal neighbors; never join pages.

items.scope_change: Use all seven pages in data/evidence/known-readings.json whose recorded method is direct: LP1-05, LP1-10 to LP1-13, LP1-16 and LP2-57. These already-readable pages replace the original LP2-00 to LP2-55 scope. Keep raw text, headings, the frozen relation and hyphen/period grouping; each page remains separate. Slashes and line breaks do not end a group.
items.limitation: This is a descriptive comparison with readable passages, not held-out validation, an independent cipher test or a significance test. It counts one frozen relation and its exact within-word rearrangement average, without repeating the original formula search or shuffled trials. These passages share manuscript spelling conventions and are not a representative language sample. Raw LP1-10 retains its archived rune order rather than the separate reviewed swap. A higher or lower count does not establish or exclude a cipher mechanism.
items.motivation: Number the runes 0–28. Count pairs six positions apart where the later number is 24 minus twice the earlier number, wrapping within 0–28. Use seven already readable pages instead of unsolved pages, keeping the earlier word grouping. Compare the count with its word-rearrangement average.

records.title: LP2-00–55: exact words and anagram repetition

records.summary: No exact repeats among 1589 or 1591 selected tokens; four length-four anagram pairs and none longer. Constrains shared word-local rules without proving plaintext repeats.
records.finding: Both boundary policies have zero exact pairs and four anagram pairs, all of length four. Shared deterministic word resets require distinct corresponding plaintext units; shared substitution plus shuffling cannot hide repeated longer words in this selection.

scope.representation: Archived rune tokens, headings retained, slash and CR/LF transparent; apostrophe boundary and transparent policies; omit first and last nonempty token per page; select ciphertext length >=4 runes.
scope.procedure: Count exact-token and named-rune anagram collisions, preserving every selected token and source offset; independently verify with regex tokenization and alphabet-count vectors.
scope.parameters: LP2-00–55; no page joining; two apostrophe policies; all selected token pairs, including within-page pairs; anagram lengths >=4 and >=5; identical function/context or shared symbol map only for the respective logical implications.
scope.exclusions: Claims that plaintext must repeat, changing effective keys or state, different word maps, alternative boundaries, page-edge tokens, language significance tests, and a general rejection of word ciphers.

records.limitations: Necessary model constraints, not a claim that plaintext repeats or all word ciphers fail. Page-edge tokens omitted. Same function/context for exact-repeat inference; same one-output-per-rune map for anagrams. Transcription dependent; human review pending.

records.title: Does the fractionation reversal undo its own shuffle?
records.question: What do the archived 6×5 keyword-grid routes produce on six intended LP2 pages, and does the archived columnar reversal invert its forward transform?
records.reader_title: Can a rune grid and rearranged coordinates decode six pages?
records.reader_intro: Uses a keyword to arrange the rune alphabet in a six-by-five grid, replaces each rune with its row and column numbers, and tests ways to rearrange or shift those numbers, including whether a shuffle can be undone.
records.reader_question: Does this grid-and-shuffle method work on LP2?
records.summary: The archived reversal fails 476 of 588 planted round trips. A repaired inverse passes all 588, but neither route yields a verified page reading under the source’s limited keyword and width grid.
records.finding: Repairing the shuffle reversal restored all planted messages, but the manuscript outputs that passed the word screen still contained invalid grid cells; none supplies a verified reading.

scope.representation: Source GP29 rune order; 6×5 keyword-first table with the last cell empty. Archived source page_38/39/40/44/45/47 rune streams independently match the corresponding current LP2 pages under the source parser.
scope.procedure: Replay split, archived column reversal, direct and coordinate-shift routes exactly. Separately correct natural-order column lengths and compare 588 full-message planted round trips.
scope.parameters: 14 source keywords; six source-intended LP2 pages; split n/n−5/n+5/n//2/2n//3; widths 7,11,13,17,19,23,29; sub/add coordinate shifts.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, keys, keyed column orders, coordinate-stream encodings, alternate null handling, source bonus running-key methods and any decryption claim.

records.limitations: Only 14 source keywords, six checked page streams, five split rules, seven natural-order column widths and two coordinate shifts. The source gate can reward a few words even when invalid cells were dropped; raw IoC is not normalized or controlled. No general fractionation or plaintext verdict.

records.title: Four archived texts as running keys
records.question: Does the source’s adaptive four-text running-key search identify a supported output on its 18 priority pages?
records.reader_question: Could Liber AL, solved text, Emerson or Deor be the key to these pages?
records.summary: The best source result was matched or beaten by 41 of 49 complete shuffled searches. The adaptive selector recovered a complete known message at a sampled offset but missed it between sampling points.
records.finding: This program found no established reading using its four proposed key texts. Its best manuscript score was matched or beaten by 41 of 49 shuffled searches. More importantly, it missed the same known message for all four texts when that message began between its sampled offsets.

scope.representation: Exact pinned source rune files for global pages21–34,43,44,49,54 matched to LP2-04–17,26–27,32,37; three exact committed text corpora plus the authored SolvedLP literal.
scope.procedure: Replay the source method-5 100-step offset/direction screen, ±100 one-direction refinement, word-plus-coincidence ranking; test four corpus plants on and off the sampling grid, one complete synthetic grid, and 49 whole-grid page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 18 pages × 4 source texts = 72 returned page/text candidates, each selected from its exact adaptive offset search; 49 full 72-candidate controls.
scope.exclusions: Other source branches, unsampled offsets not promoted by the source, other corpora/editions, resets, interruptions, alternate scoring and complete decryptors.

records.limitations: The source samples key offsets every 100 positions, then refines only around the best coincidence and only in its chosen direction. An unchanged known reading planted at offset 137 was missed for every text. records.title: Short seeds for autokey ciphers
records.question: Do the pinned source keyword, two-rune, or three-rune autokey seeds pass their one-rune and IoC screens on the selected LP2 pages?
records.reader_title: Can earlier runes extend a short starting key?
records.reader_intro: Tries named words and two- or three-rune starting keys that grow using earlier encrypted or recovered runes, plus a separate four-rune key spelling DEOR, not the text of the Old English poem.
records.reader_question: Could a short word or rune seed drive an autokey cipher?
records.summary: Four related archived search branches were replayed on verified LP2 page streams. None passed the source-defined hit screen; the gate and ciphertext-feedback design sharply limit what that result can exclude.
records.finding: None of the tested seeds passed the source’s screening rule. The distinct four-rune DEOR seed covered only ten pages, and the source did not test word resets. Its controls recovered a planted reading in all six feedback modes.

scope.representation: Pinned archived source GP29 page values verified against current LP2-04–37 text; source pages old21–54 map to LP2-(old−17). Source isolated-word positions retained.
scope.procedure: Replay six GP29 plaintext/ciphertext feedback recurrences for 22 source keyword seeds, every two-rune seed, every three-rune seed on source-eligible pages, and the one distinct four-rune P21–30 DEOR array. Preserve source gates, strict IoC threshold and page resets; compare 49 full-search shuffles.
scope.parameters: 4,488 named-keyword, 171,564 two-rune, 4,536,354 three-rune, and 60 distinct P21–30 DEOR settings; 49 within-page shuffled complete searches, seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other seeds or lengths, alternate alphabets, word resets and segmentations, different singleton assumptions, English scoring, the P21–30 running-key/double-layer branches, and manuscript-derived numerical autokey rules without an exact recurrence.

records.limitations: The source requires visible one-rune words to decode to I or A, which assumes this word segmentation and language. Ciphertext-feedback seeds alter only their own short output prefix, so the whole-page screen cannot reliably identify those seeds. Forty-nine full-search shuffles are coarse controls, not a cipher model. Other seed lengths, pages, boundaries and autokey rules remain untested.

records.title: Archived Cicada numbers and byte streams as LP2 keys
records.question: Do 25 archived number or byte sources recover LP2 under the pinned phase-averaged stay/advance/skip key detector?
records.reader_question: Do Cicada number and byte streams work as LP2 keys?
records.summary: Exact accelerated replay of the pinned Stage R source grid finds no candidate above its declared +30 line; all planted controls pass.
records.finding: All 43,500 LP2 candidate rows and 200 control rows match the pinned source tables at published 0.01-nat precision. No LP2 setting reaches +30. The highest score, +2.41, is on the nine-rune title; its absolute score ceiling is only +11.19, so its 4,350 settings could never pass. The best other section scores −50.75, and the complete joined text peaks at −1,479.67. Correct-key planted controls score at least +169.09 and wrong-key controls at most −60.86. The compiled scorer agrees with the source on real and synthetic parity cases.

scope.representation: Source GP29 rune transcript in sections 7–15 and their continuous join, covering unsolved LP2-00–55; section labels are not manuscript page numbers.
scope.procedure: Read 25 pinned number/byte sources into modulo-29 and rejection-mapped key streams. For each of 50 keys and ten section alignments, score three arithmetic modes and all 29 shifts with the pinned phase-averaged stay/advance/skip HMM. Replay 200 planted positive/negative pairs with exact seed. Compare all serialized rows against the pinned Stage R tables.
scope.parameters: 50 mapped streams × 10 alignments × 3 modes × 29 shifts = 43,500 source settings; +30-nat pass line; uniform cyclic phase, transition 0.02/0.96/0.02, epsilon 0.1, pruning 1e−12. Control lengths 729 and 3316, fresh/next rekey, keep 0.19, RNG seed 3301.
scope.exclusions: Other source bytes, ordering, mapping, page segmentation, selected rather than averaged phase, alternative drift/rekey model, key operations, plaintext prior or downstream layer.

records.limitations: The nine-rune title is too short for this +30 threshold under any key, so those 4,350 settings are not informative negatives. This screen uses only the source's 25 inputs, two GP29 mappings, ten transcript alignments, three arithmetic modes, 29 shifts, solved-LP1 unigram model, drift probabilities and uniform start-phase prior. Controls show power for this generated model at two longer lengths, not for every LP2 construction. Other preprocessing, keys, schedules, language models and cipher layers remain untested.

records.title: Can a guessed word seed a short feedback key?
records.question: Does a source-defined crib-derived GF(29) linear recurrence predict a language-like 128-rune continuation on 11 named unsolved LP2 pages when the key phase and J-rune parsing are corrected?
records.reader_question: Could a guessed word reveal the key for the following runes?
records.summary: The corrected crib rule produced 13 two-rune-validated candidate fits, but its best 128-rune continuation scored 18; 126 of 199 complete shuffled searches did at least as well. A separate post-result known-reading plant ranked first across a mixed 11-page search in all 12 mode/order cases, showing this exact screen can detect a clean positive.
records.finding: The best continuation from the guessed words scored no better than many shuffled pages: 126 of 199 shuffled searches matched or exceeded it. A separate planted known reading was recovered correctly.

scope.representation: Pinned source page-number mapping separately preserves the source's J-dropping rune sequence on 11 LP2 pages plus solved LP1-15. Corrected scan uses canonical GP29 site arrays for the 11 LP2 pages; each source array equals its canonical counterpart with J removed.
scope.procedure: Replay the source's original crib-drag Berlekamp-Massey and IoC gate. Separately fit the first m-2 key symbols from each selected source crib, verify the last two, predict the next 128 runes and score only that continuation; rerun the complete page/crib/mode/offset selection on 199 shared seeded page shuffles.
scope.parameters: Original 21 source cribs length>=4, 3 directions and 12 mapped pages; corrected 13 source cribs length>=6, 3 directions, recurrence order 2–5, all offsets leaving 128 runes, 11 LP2 pages; 199 shuffle trials seed 20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other LP2 pages, other cribs, order>5, non-GP alphabets, key skips/resets, unrelated recurrence laws, a trained language model, and proof of full decryption.

records.limitations: The original source gate scores a page containing its own guessed crib and uses a rune parser that drops J. The corrected search still covers only 13 words, feedback lengths 2–5, three arithmetic directions, 11 pages and one approximate GP bigram/trigram score. The page-frequency shuffle is not a cipher generator. The post-result positive is one known 226-rune reading under a clean page-local clock, shorter than the replaced 273-rune LP2 page, and cannot prove power against every LP2 plaintext. No LFSR family or alternate key clock is excluded.

records.summary: The source gate raw IoC >1.3 is impossible. Under a separately frozen normalized-IoC amendment, the complete 102,036-setting source grid produces no score over 1.3; 157 of 199 full-search shuffles reach at least the observed maximum.
records.finding: After the corrected score gate, 3,031 settings pass the source singleton filter and none exceeds 1.3. The global maximum is 1.226492057 on LP2-14. records.question: Do the six fixed aligned-copy regions in three pinned Wulfic legacy scripts exist on their verified LP2 input, and what does the separate page-pair difference screen show?

records.summary: The three scripts’ specific identical-span premises fail on their committed source pages; a separate page-pair frequency screen does not establish key reuse.
records.finding: The proposed matching passages do not match. Five of the six pairs extend beyond the supplied text; the remaining pair agrees at only 7 of 404 rune positions. The separate page-pair search also missed most known examples of key reuse.

scope.representation: Corrected source old page_21–54 = LP2-04–37, GP29 rune-only, continuous 8,226-rune stream. Label-disambiguation check on LP2-27 and LP2-44. Four direct-reading LP1 pages provide matched-length planted pairs.
scope.procedure: Check all six source asserted identical regions, the claimed page27/page44 prefix and period bounds on the original committed Git page objects; replay the separate all-page-pair ±IoC source function, then 199 whole-search page-wise shuffles and all ten fixed 137-rune shared-key plants.
scope.parameters: Six asserted regions, one 6,726-rune period, 34 pages, 561 unordered pairs ×2 operations=1,122 screens, IoC>1.15, 199 seeded full-search shuffles (seed20261023), five 137-rune reading windows forming ten fixed pairs.
scope.exclusions: Unknown key-reuse alignments or periods, arbitrary key clocks, crib readability scoring under the failed source-copy assumption, alternative transcriptions, and separate solved/reference-text running-key branches.

records.limitations: This falsifies six named identical-ciphertext premises, not general shared-key encryption: equal keys can yield different ciphertexts when plaintexts differ, and equal ciphertext alone does not prove equal keys. All 34 source page blobs exist in Git despite the sparse local checkout and match the site pages; the source pair-score functions were replayed exactly. The period and crib loops based on the failed alignments are not meaningful complete decoding tests. The page-pair controls were added after preliminary outcomes were viewed. Page shuffling preserves unigram counts, not natural plaintext, and the IoC screen misses most planted reuse pairs at length 137. Running-key branches of one source script are separate from this grouped claim.
